qa.question: Birth
qa.answer:
For a birth or adoption, you can:
• Add your child to medical, dental, and vision coverage.
• Consider a dependent care FSA if you will have childcare costs.
• Update your life insurance beneficiaries.
• Review parental leave options.

You must make these changes within [CONFIRM: 30/60] days of the birth or adoption. After that, you generally must wait until the next open enrollment.

You’ll likely need a birth certificate or adoption paperwork.

Would you like to know how this affects your FSA or HSA, or see what documents you’ll need?
followUps: How does this affect my FSA or HSA?

qa.question: What’s the deadline?
qa.answer: For this life event, you must make benefit changes within [CONFIRM: 30/60] days from the event date. If you miss this window, you usually must wait until the next open enrollment unless another qualifying event occurs.

qa.question: What documents do I need?
qa.answer:
For [selected event], typical documents include:
• Birth or adoption certificate (for new child)
• Marriage certificate (for adding a spouse)
• Divorce decree (for removing a spouse)
• Proof of loss of coverage letter (for losing other coverage)

You’ll upload these in the benefits portal or provide them to HR if requested.
